- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.16 or lower) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 30d mean), reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to prevent overshoot; sentiment spikes often indicate temporary volatility, not sustained trend.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.27 or near-zero), model often overestimates mean reversion; cap forecast at 1–2 std dev above recent 18-day average to avoid overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon when sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.27) — increase forecast by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops) and sentiment is negative, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — add 3–5% upward bias to avoid “stuck in trough” error.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is significantly below model (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior — if so, model may have overreacted to sentiment; reduce forecast by 3–7% to align with sentiment decay.
